dateRule: Each entry's date is the earliest publicly verifiable appearance of the primary source that introduced the technique in the form, and under the name, the field now uses: for arXiv papers, the v1 'Submitted on' date on the arXiv abstract page (not the later conference date); for forum posts and releases, the first-party post or announcement date. Earlier work that computes substantially the same operation in another setting (for example inside an RNN or a memory network) is listed as an 'earlier root' with its own verified date and shown on the card, rather than silently moving the date or hiding it. Adoption dates mark the first verified use in a notable released model and are reported separately.
effectsKey: Effects are judged against the default of the moment (dense causal softmax attention as practised when the entry appeared; for the 2014 entry, an RNN encoder-decoder). +2 relieves that bill a lot, -2 makes it markedly worse or gives up a lot of it.

entries.name: Additive attention for translation
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio

source.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

precursors.title: Graves, 'Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks' — a soft, differentiable window over the input for handwriting synthesis
precursors.note: An earlier soft attention-like read; Bahdanau et al. is the version that launched attention in NLP.

entries.notes: Included as the prologue: the problem it fixed (squeezing a whole sentence into one fixed-size vector) is the problem linear attention and DeltaNet later re-accept on purpose. Luong et al. (arXiv:1508.04025, 2015-08-17) added multiplicative scoring and a windowed 'local attention'.

entries.name: Learned absolute position embeddings
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Gehring et al., “A Convolutional Encoder Model for Neural Machine Translation”, which adds learned position embeddings for the absolute position of each source word

source.title: A Convolutional Encoder Model for Neural Machine Translation

precursors.title: End-To-End Memory Networks (Sukhbaatar et al.) — learned 'temporal encoding' rows indexed by memory slot
precursors.note: Learned per-slot vectors that index memory sentences rather than token positions; Gehring et al. cite memory networks as the inspiration.

adoption.what: ConvS2S (Gehring et al.) — the paper the Transformer cites for learned positional embeddings
Attention Is All You Need tries learned embeddings and reports results 'nearly identical' to sinusoids (Table 3, row E)
GPT-1 uses learned position embeddings 'instead of the sinusoidal version'
adoption.note: Release date as reported by web search of OpenAI's page (the page returned HTTP 403 to our fetchers); the quoted sentence was read in OpenAI's PDF.

adoption.what: BERT (position embeddings learned during pretraining up to 512 positions)

entries.notes: The first audit pass dated this to ConvS2S (May 2017); the independent audit found this earlier paper by the same group, which does the same thing, so the date moved back six months.

entries.name: Scaled dot-product attention (with multi-head and the causal mask)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of 'Attention Is All You Need'

source.title: Attention Is All You Need
source.authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin

precursors.title: Additive attention over RNN states (Bahdanau et al.)
precursors.note: Attention as a helper to a recurrent network.

precursors.title: Luong et al. — dot-product ('multiplicative') attention scores
precursors.note: Dot-product scoring predates the Transformer; the scaling by 1/√dₖ, multi-head attention and an attention-only network are what is new in 2017.

precursors.title: Parikh et al. — intra-sentence (self-)attention
precursors.note: Tokens attending to tokens of the same sentence, before the Transformer.

entries.notes: What is new in 2017 is the scaling by 1/√dₖ, multi-head attention and a network built from attention alone; dot-product scores and self-attention both existed earlier (see earlier roots).

entries.name: Sinusoidal position encoding
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of 'Attention Is All You Need' (same paper as scaled dot-product attention)

source.title: Attention Is All You Need

precursors.title: End-To-End Memory Networks: a fixed, computed 'position encoding' for word order inside a sentence
precursors.note: A computed (not learned) position weighting existed earlier, but not a sinusoidal signal for sequence positions in an attention model.

entries.notes: The authors chose sinusoids because they hypothesised the model 'may' extrapolate to longer sequences — a hypothesis, not a demonstrated property.

entries.name: Relative position representations
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani

source.title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

precursors.title: Parikh et al. — distance-sensitive bias terms inside intra-sentence attention
precursors.note: An earlier relative-distance term in attention.

entries.notes: Added because it is the step that brought relative distance into Transformer self-attention — the line RoPE and ALiBi continue.

entries.name: Segment recurrence (Transformer-XL)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Dai et al.

source.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
source.authors: Dai, Yang, Yang, Carbonell, Le, Salakhutdinov

entries.notes: Added as the first widely cited answer to 'what crosses the window boundary?' — the question memory-stream designs return to.

entries.name: Fixed sparse attention patterns (Sparse Transformer)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Child, Gray, Radford & Sutskever

source.title: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers

precursors.title: Generating Wikipedia by Summarizing Long Sequences — local attention blocks and memory-compressed attention
precursors.note: Earlier restriction of which pairs are computed.

precursors.title: Image Transformer — blocks of local attention
precursors.note: Local 1D/2D attention for images.

adoption.what: GPT-3 uses 'alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention patterns ... similar to the Sparse Transformer'

entries.notes: This is “sparse attention” in its first factorized, Transformer-scale form: which pairs are computed is decided by position, not content.

entries.name: Multi-query attention (MQA)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Shazeer, 'One Write-Head is All You Need'

source.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

entries.name: Top-k attention (Explicit Sparse Transformer)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Zhao et al.

source.title: Explicit Sparse Transformer: Concentrated Attention Through Explicit Selection
source.authors: Zhao, Lin, Zhang, Ren, Su, Sun

precursors.title: Rae et al., Sparse Access Memory — reads only the K nearest memory words
precursors.note: Top-K reads in a memory-augmented network.

precursors.title: Sparse Attentive Backtracking (Ke et al.) — 'selects and normalizes only the k top greatest raw attention weights' over past RNN states
precursors.note: The same top-k-then-renormalise operation, in an RNN; cited by Zhao et al.

adoption.what: Content-based sparse siblings (not adoptions): Reformer (LSH buckets)
Routing Transformer (k-means routing)
DeepSeek-V3.2: a lightning indexer chooses 2,048 key-value tokens per query (released as V3.2-Exp on 2025-09-29)

entries.notes: Top-k selection inside Transformer attention appears in 2019, with the same operation in RNN and memory models in 2016–2018. The 2019 paper’s motivation was concentration (quality), not speed: it still scored every key. What 2025 adds (NSA, DSA) is a cheap trained selector that makes the selection pay for itself at scale.

entries.name: Linear attention
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Katharopoulos et al., 'Transformers are RNNs'

source.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention

precursors.title: Efficient Attention: Attention with Linear Complexities (Shen et al.)
precursors.note: Reorders the product to avoid the T×T matrix, using separate normalisations of Q and K; vision-focused and not framed as a causal recurrent state.

precursors.title: Fast-weight memories (Schmidhuber, Neural Computation 1992)
precursors.note: The 'sum of outer products as memory' idea; bibliographic details from library records, not a fetched first page.

adoption.what: Siblings the same year: Linformer (low-rank projection, a different idea)
Performer (random-feature softmax approximation)

entries.name: The delta rule for linear attention
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Schlag, Irie & Schmidhuber, which introduces the delta-rule update for linear Transformers

precursors.title: Widrow & Hoff, 'Adaptive switching circuits' (IRE WESCON) — the delta / LMS learning rule
precursors.note: The rule itself is from 1960 (bibliographic record, not a fetched copy). What 2021 adds is using it as the write rule of a linear-attention memory.

entries.name: FlashAttention (IO-aware exact attention)
entries.dateEvent: arXiv v1 of Dao et al.

entries.notes: Not in the core list, and arguably the most consequential omission: it changed which bill mattered by making exact attention cheap in memory traffic, without approximating anything. Activation memory becomes linear in sequence length, but the FLOP count is still quadratic and the inference KV cache is unchanged.

entries.name: Compressed Sparse + Heavily Compressed Attention (DeepSeek-V4)
entries.dateEvent: DeepSeek-V4 Preview release announcement (DeepSeek API docs news)

source.title: DeepSeek-V4 Preview release

precursors.title: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (V3.2-Exp)
NSA's compressed-token branch

adoption.what: Technical report on arXiv

entries.notes: The release page says only “token-wise compression + DSA”; the names CSA and HCA and all numbers come from the technical report (“DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence”, arXiv:2606.19348, v1 submitted 26 April 2026 — two days after the release; the ID prefix is unusual for an April submission but the abstract page states this date). From the report: CSA compresses every 4 tokens into one entry and applies DSA-style top-k (k = 1,024 for V4-Pro, 512 for V4-Flash) plus a 128-token uncompressed window; HCA compresses 128 tokens per entry and attends densely; CSA and HCA layers are interleaved; RoPE is applied to the last 64 dimensions. At 1M tokens the report gives V4-Pro 27% of V3.2’s single-token FLOPs and 10% of its KV cache (V4-Flash: 10% and 7%).
